[Music] My name is Lissy, and I come from the USA. First of all, I offer a thousand thanks to
my mother and the Holy Trinity for giving me the opportunity to come to this stage and share my testimony.
On June 23, 2024, in Canada, Joseph Father’s covenant class was held. That is where we took our covenant. Father came there,
and we attended the two-day covenant classes and covenant meditation. We also took our covenant there. My family and I participated fully.
If I were to describe the first intention, it was incredibly miraculous. Through a short period of time, God
and Mother gave us a blessing that we could fully experience. That intention was not done with full faith at first.
The reason I took it was because I am a nurse who completed my nursing studies in 2004–2005. At that time, the USA
was a place where every nurse wanted to go, and it was open to all. Other countries were not that open at that time.
From then on, I passed all my IELTS exams on the first attempt and also cleared CGFNS.
Even though I passed all the ENCLEx exams and everything else, my paperwork was always
a major obstacle. As I tried to move forward, it kept getting more and more complicated.
Around 2007, I gave up on going to the USA. By 2011, we moved to Canada, and we have been
in Canada for the past 14 years. When the USA opened again in 2017, I applied to go there once more.
My paperwork still didn’t go through. There were countless obstacles that no one could explain—not even I
could understand why there were so many barriers. So I put it aside, thinking I could go someday.
For now, we are in Canada. I thought maybe God didn’t want me to go to the USA.
During last year’s covenant, Father said something that really struck me: “Do not put in
your covenant intentions you are sure will happen. Put in what you think will not happen.”
That’s why I took it as a challenge. I wanted to know what Father would say. I didn’t initially
plan to mention it in my first testimony. I didn’t need to talk about the USA project to Father.
Like everyone else, I have many problems. We can list them, but to receive the blessed medal
when I went near Father, even for a second or five seconds, He gives us time to speak.
When I went near Father, the thought came to me: “Father, I have been trying
for the last 18 years for the USA, but it’s not happening. I don’t know why.”
Father looked at me, and after just one glance, He responded.
He just asked me to close my eyes and look, then placed His
hand on my head and prayed for me, and told me what to do.
Then I returned and took the covenant—it was a very beautiful experience. I prayed, took the covenant, and came home.
At home, I thought: in case the US embassy calls me for an
interview, even with the normal process, our embassy’s queue would be for 2027.
There are still many obstacles for me. Even if these obstacles are removed
and the normal process starts, I would only get an interview in 2027.
I stayed at home and continued the apparition prayers very actively. My husband
and I go to church, read the Bible, and follow what Father said.
Many changes came into our lives: we learned to forgive those who are hard to forgive, to love others, and to accept others.
After taking a covenant and two days at home, a thought came to me from within: to write a letter.
I felt as if Mother was speaking to me from within, telling me to write a letter to the US embassy.
Writing a letter is not a small thing to the embassy, but given my background—without any connections, applying
for a US visa or green card for many years—it was not a small matter.
I asked Mother about it, and the instruction was clear: “write a letter.”
This letter was just an email, not a professional formal letter. I opened my email and wrote what Mother guided me from within.
I wrote a prayerful email for a person at the embassy, praying the apparition prayer seven times as
I wrote. I had no idea who the person was, or which family it was for.
This letter represents a dream I tried to pursue when I was 18–20 years old, right after finishing my nursing studies.
My US migration journey has now taken 10, 15, almost 18 years. My daughter is now 18,
and still, I wondered: why is this not happening for me? Why am I facing so many obstacles?
There are reasons, but not valid reasons for them to grant me a visa. Another reason: my
daughter wants to enter a university, and if I could provide the opportunity, she could study there.
But that is not a valid reason. As a Canadian citizen, sending my child to study in the US is possible. So that is not a valid reason either.
I wrote these two reasons, prayed before Mother, and sent the letter.
Two days later, on a Tuesday at 2:30, I got a message back.
The US embassy accepted the letter and sent my paperwork to them so I could get an interview as soon as possible.
I felt like I had stepped into a time machine.
Then Mother told me that my interview would come, with medical checks scheduled weeks apart.
My covenant would be completed 90 days before, and my husband, my children, and I would receive the US green card at our home.
I didn’t know that anyone who had gone through the US process would understand how hard migration to that country is.
It’s not just five or ten years—I have done many meditations and fasts. I’m not someone who hasn’t practiced austerity and meditation.
But Mother walked with me and took me to that country. It was a place I could never have applied to myself, some unknown location.
Yet, it was a very beautiful town. Mother guided me and arranged everything there.
Even after arriving, it was March when we moved. My husband and children joined me last month.
After that, to share my testimony, I prayed to Mother for permission.
“Mother, this is a miracle. If I am to give testimony, I can only do it here.”
I had entered a new hospital, a place where normally I wouldn’t get any
leave. But my manager gave me two weeks’ leave so I could give testimony.
We all came together, and this was my first very miraculous experience.
My Kreupasanam Mother opened my eyes and led me wonderfully through this time.
The second miracle: my husband had been in Canada, struggling with work for eight years.
Every year there would be a different job.
Nothing was permanent. After a year, either the position would end, hours would reduce, or they’d say they didn’t need him.
This happened for eight years, and during the last covenant meditation, we prayed:
“Mother, now give him a good, stable job without further changes.”
As a result, he was given a permanent position in the local Catholic school board.
It was miraculous. It wasn’t a job we could have gotten on our
own, but through prayer, all obstacles were removed, and it came to us.
I offer immense thanks to Mother and Jesus for this.
Through this covenant, many changes have come to us. As Father says, when we do the covenant properly, we ourselves change.
Many differences emerge. Maybe we feel ourselves becoming better people; when we look back, we are no longer the old person, but a new one.
We hesitate less to make mistakes, and with Mother’s presence, I, as a nurse,
feel that when I approach each patient, I can care for them with great love.
After taking the covenant, I have experienced a change in myself. Mother has given
me the grace to love others more and to accept them as they are.
This is a great blessing that everyone who takes the covenant receives.
Regarding my missionary work: mainly, it is distributing newsletters. Even though I am Malayali, I
don’t distribute them to just anyone in Malayalam. I give them to colleagues from other countries.
Father often said that just giving a leaflet randomly doesn’t matter.
So, I go to many English-speaking churches and sit there. I find it difficult to approach people
directly, so I pray: “God, Jesus, Mother, please show me the person who should receive this newsletter.”
Then I tell those present what it is, and some will listen attentively. They
read the newsletter and learn about the covenant prayer and how to take it.
It brings me immense joy. Explaining it to someone who knows nothing is a tremendous happiness.
I also have some friends in the Philippines. Mother has specially instructed me to take photos of Her and bring them to everyone.
No matter who comes from back home, I ensure they get it immediately. Sometimes I drive three or four hours to deliver newsletters and photos.
They haven’t seen this blue-grey Mother in person. When asked, I explain everything in English so they understand.
Father told me to have a non-Malayali person take the covenant, and doing this is a great honor.
The joy I get after doing this is tremendous. After the covenant, many people receive blessings through it.
I can say that I have helped many people take the covenant and receive blessings through it.
My friends have also come here, come to Alappuzha, prayed the covenant, and done everything.
No matter how much I praise Jesus and Mother for all this, it
is never enough. I thank Mother for giving me the opportunity to stand here.
Even last week, I never imagined I would come to Kreupasanam and give testimony on this
stage. I am very grateful to Mother for arranging this. Praise, glory, and honor to Jesus.
My name is Yesudas. When my wife suggested taking the covenant prayer, I had
never agreed before. There were many obstacles, and she said we must follow it.
Later, one day, I lit our light a candle. After that, I myself started the covenant prayer.
Then many people were able to take the covenant. We use holy salt in many ways.
That means whatever paperwork we complete, whatever exams we finish, we use the holy salt.
Even on our mobile phones or laptops, we apply the holy salt. Then we say a a apparition prayer, and that’s how we do all these things.
Similarly, when children fall sick, the first thing I do is use the covenant oil.
Many people have been able to come and take the covenant. Even my
family, after I took the covenant, were able to come and take it.
I also brought my friends, and they have all received many blessings from Mother directly.
Many who were blocked by paperwork and could not go out are now free. They come willingly to take the covenant.
This is the experience we see in life after taking the covenant. Mother has greatly blessed our family.
I am thankful to Mother for allowing us to come and give testimony here.
Psalm 28: “The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusts in Him, and I am helped.”
That is why I receive help; my heart rejoices. I sing praises and thank Him there.
Lisimol and Yesudas, under the protection of Mother, are giving testimony of the great divine experiences received through the Kreupasanam covenant.
We are testifying at this altar with gratitude for these immense divine experiences. For 18 years, I have longed for US migration,
but it was blocked in ways that seemed impossible. Even when seeing my father, I did not wish to speak about it, yet
in a split second—just five seconds—I could convey the message to my father, as if that last moment was one single sentence.
Father says that US migration hasn’t been happening for years. He takes a look—that’s basically what happened.
But what we see entirely is Mother—everything, tears, messages, and life matters are entrusted into Mother’s hands.
Within a short span of about two or three months, she arranged everything so securely
that US migration became a reality.
She prepared the ways for the family to reach together and blessed the family. This is the testimony of that blessing.
Prayer should never be neglected. Any intention or matter that is entrusted into Mother’s hands with tears,
she takes it to Jesus, blesses it, and turns it into a grace for us. That is why, when we enter into the covenant,
just as Lisimol indicated, our lives change, our attitudes change, and our relationships change.
Each of us becomes more holy, more God-loving, and more capable of caring for others.
This, in the presence of God, becomes a reason for Him to intervene and pour out His grace as a great blessing.
God’s time is not like our time; in His eyes, what seems like a thousand years is as a single moment.
Therefore, when we place something in Mother’s hands, knowing this, she receives it, and the pilgrim Mother
fully trusts and believes that it will become the cause of grace within a short time. This is what the daughter says.
One day, a message arrived—it was meant to send an email to the embassy. She didn’t know who exactly to send it to,
didn’t know what to write, or why it needed to be sent, but the message clearly instructed: send the email.
She explained the entire email to us. There wasn’t any valid reason for it,
but according to the covenant, Mother had passed a communication to us. It could happen through people, through words, through dreams,
or through certain interventions. If even one message is passed, it has the power
to become a sign, a marker toward the fruitfulness of that intention, the daughter says.
This one email helped to take the matter up very quickly
and to accelerate her visa process. Within a few months, two or three
months, she said the covenant opened the way for her to receive the visa
and reach America even before the covenant’s time period was completed. Dear friends,
the covenant is not a small matter. The covenant deals with seemingly impossible matters.
Do we write it down? Do we fully surrender to Mother with complete faith?
Are we ready to arrange our lives accordingly? Mother allows us great experiences within short periods of time,
and we can see how these turn into Jesus’ blessings. That is the great testimony this family is sharing from this altar.
Let us clap our hands in gratitude, offering this testimony for all the goodness and blessings received by this family,
and for the faith and trust placed in Mother.
